comparison_rule: Every experiment is compared with the EVALUATED hotel's seasonal_naive_7 on the identical paired rows (both forecast). Wins, losses and ties on absolute error; win_proportion = wins / paired; differences learned - baseline. No threshold, no winner, no pooled headline: validation and test are reported separately and never combined.

label: diagnostic single-hotel models, fitted in memory and discarded; none is the served artifact and none is a candidate
limitations: Same source: two Portuguese hotels, 2015-2017, one published dataset. Nothing here establishes generalisation to other hotels or production accuracy.
Single-hotel models are fitted on about half the rows of the served pooled model (414 and 402 vs 816); they are diagnostics, not candidates, and none is served.
The two hotels' eligible training rows differ by 12 (the resort hotel's data starts 12 days later); the difference is recorded, not equalised.
Not pristine: these months were seen by the Stage 6.3 backtest and by R2.2. Nothing was tuned on them.
Two hotels give one same-hotel/cross-hotel contrast per evaluated hotel; there is no third.
The lag ranges were chosen from a description of the training partition; groups with fewer than 30 paired rows report counts only.
Point forecasts only; no interval and no significance test.
range_rule: A prediction is outside the training-target range when it is strictly below the minimum or strictly above the maximum target_room_nights among the rows the model was fitted on. A prediction equal to either bound is inside. fraction_outside = (below + above) / paired.
sign_convention: signed error = prediction - actual. Positive means over-prediction, negative means under-prediction. mean_signed_error is the plain mean over the paired rows.
